source.title: Stability and Generalization of Learning Algorithms that Converge to Global Optima

record.tranche_reason: The paper develops theoretical stability bounds and a toy counterexample, but does not test any listed version's natural-label train/test generalization claim.
record.gate_note: The paper cites empirical generalization findings from other work; those cited results are not extracted as rows. Its own SGD/GD results concern stability on a constructed non-convex problem, not the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper derives stability bounds and constructs an SGD–GD stability comparison. It does not measure any listed version's behavior: in particular, its batch comparison establishes stability rather than held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors derive convergence-based stability bounds under PL/QG assumptions and construct a nonconvex example where SGD is stable but GD is not. They explicitly leave open whether SGD generally produces more generalizable models than GD.
record.recipe_differences: Theoretical stability analysis under PL/QG conditions, plus a constructed toy-network example; it does not use the empirical recipes in the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The constructed SGD result specifies step size γ = 1 and initialization near ŵ; the GD instability result holds for 0 < γ ≤ 1 and a non-zero measure set of starting points.

fits_no_version.finding: For constructed neighboring datasets and specified initializations, GD has a loss difference of at least 1/2 after sufficiently many iterations, whereas SGD has an expected loss-difference bound of O(1/n) under the stated convergence conditions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD can be stable on a constructed nonconvex quadratic-network problem where full-batch GD is unstable.

record.problems: The optimizer comparison is a constructed theoretical example, not an empirical comparison on natural-label benchmarks. The paper says the breadth of the SGD stability phenomenon remains unclear.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on random versus natural labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed to fit training data.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across training-set sizes and regularization recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness rankings of measured generalization gaps and comparison with other measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The discussion of sharpness is speculative, and the large-batch generalization findings are cited from prior work. Neither supplies an additional test of the listed versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test performance.
Network-width sweep and test error beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum on held-out benchmarks.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and measured generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples and its effect on test accuracy.

rows.note: The authors contrast this stability result with gradient descent's instability in the constructed setting.
rows.check: The O(1/n) bound correctly records Theorem 6.2's expected signed loss difference. The supporting argument permits decreasing the step size after the initial γ=1 step and assumes convergence within 1/n of a local minimum; the row should preserve this qualification rather than imply a demonstrated constant-step convergence guarantee. Stability does not measure any listed version.
